newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek troops will go to Albania's port of Vlore.
newsitem.headline: Greek troops will go to Albania's port of Vlore.

text.p: Some of the Greek troops in a multinational security force planned for neighbouring Albania will be deployed in the rebel-held Adriatic port of Vlore, a defence ministry spokesman said on Tuesday.
The 6,000-strong Italian-led force, being sent to protect humanitarian aid, is expected to start its mission in the lawless Balkan state around April 14.
Most of the Greek contingent, about 700 soldiers, will be sent to Tirana but the rest will be sent to the southern port which has been under rebel control since February, the spokesman said.

Vlore was swept by anti-Italian sentiment late last month after the sinking of an Albanian refugee boat which collided with an Italian navy ship. Albania says at least 80 people died, most from Vlore.
The port is also considered one of the most dangerous tasks of the multinational force because local rebel leaders have no organised armed group.
Albania's second most active port, Vlore has been closed for weeks after leading a popular uprising against President Sali Berisha.
Local residents, at the forefront of the campaign against Berisha, drove out police and military units and later seized large stocks of weapons from army depots.
The campaign against Berisha began in January when a series of popular, but fraudulent, investment schemes collapsed, wiping out millions of dollars in savings.
